summary: A Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar, Shudo Ishii earned a BA at Komazawa University (~1961–1965) and studied under Shigeo Kamata. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1988–2016).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shudo Iwai completed doctoral coursework at Komazawa University. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University, attested in 1988.

Shuhong Chang worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Zhejiang Sci-Tech University (~1918–1923) and Zhejiang University, and served as director of the Dunhuang Academy from around 1944 to 1982.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Shuji Takayama held posts at Ryukoku University (part-time lecturer) and Bukkyo University (research fellow) in 2003, and at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College and Musashino University in 2006.

Working in Indology and philosophy, Shujun Motegi studied under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi at Banaras Hindu University (1973–1975) and earned an MA from Kyoto University by 1977. He served at Shinshu University, attested as Professor of Ethics in 2010.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Shuken Ito completed graduate studies at Komazawa University (attested 1973). He served at Komazawa University as a research assistant (attested 1973–1978) and professor (attested 1994), and also held a post at Aichi Gakuin University.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Shuman Chen studied under traditional teacher Wei Chueh and completed a PhD at Northwestern University by 2014 under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, Shun'ei Hirai studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo (~1955–1961). He served as a professor at Komazawa University from around 1965 to 2001.
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shun'ei Matsushita served at Otani University as a term-limited assistant professor until 2013 and as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Shunkyo Katsumata studied at the University of Tokyo (~1930–1934). He held posts at Toyo University and Taisho University, where he was attested as professor emeritus in 1981–1982.
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shunpaku Nakao served at Shuchiin University as an assistant professor (attested 1963) and as a professor (attested 1976).
A philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar, Shunpei Ueyama studied at Kyoto University from around 1940 to 1943 and later held a post there from around 1954 to 1984.

A Buddhist studies figure, Shunryu Suzuki studied under Gyokujun So-on (~1917–1926), Ian Kishizawa, and at Komazawa University (~1926–1930). He founded the San Francisco Zen Center and the Tassajara Zen Mountain Center.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology, Shunsho Manabe studied at Tohoku University. He held posts at Hosen Gakuen College and Shikoku University, where he was attested as professor in 2015.
A Buddhist studies scholar, Shunshō Terakawa studied at the University of Tokyo. He held a post as emeritus professor at Otani University, attested from 1998 to 2006.
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shuntaro Kondo earned a PhD from Ryukoku University by 2011 and served there as a part-time lecturer in 2012.

An Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, Shuntaro Matsuyama studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1956). He held posts at Kokugakuin University, Tama Art University, and Joshibi University of Art and Design, where he was a professor (attested 1994).

A Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar, Shunzo Onoda completed a D.Lit. at Bukkyo University by 1993. He served at Bukkyo University as associate professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2005).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, Shuyu Kanaoka studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1954). He served as assistant professor (~1961–1966) and professor (~1966–1993) at Toyo University, and as professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1962).

A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, Shōkin Furuta studied at Shimane University. He served as director of Matsugaoka Bunko (~1980–2001) and held posts attested in 1998 at Hokkaido University and Nihon University.
